newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Six hurt in Tel Aviv blasts - minister.
newsitem.headline: Six hurt in Tel Aviv blasts - minister.

text.p: Two bombs apparently planted by Arab guerrillas exploded near Tel Aviv's central bus station on Thursday, wounding at least six people, Israel's police minister said.

"There were two explosions, not big ones, on Neve Sheanan street. There are six people wounded, most of them slightly," Avigdor Kahalani told Israeli Army Radio. Asked if police believed Arab guerrillas were responsible for the blasts, he said: "That's what we think."
Kahalani said it appeared the bombs were planted in trash cans in the area.
The blasts came against the backdrop of U.S.-brokered talks between Israel and the PLO on self-rule for most of the West Bank town of Hebron.
Palestinian militants last mounted a bombing campaign in the Jewish state in February and March when suicide bombers killed 59 people.
"There was a very strong explosion under the Central Cinema, in a snack bar. A few minutes later, there was another blast," a witness told Israeli Army Radio.

"It was a tremendous explosion. A sunflower seed seller was hurt. Police arrived five minutes later. As they were checking things, another bomb went off and a policeman was hurt," said another witness.
